text: mira: Quick sync — design review for capacity controls heuristics. Posted updated mockups and a decision tree here: https://figma.com/file/xxx. Need input on: min/max wording, burst affordance, GPU pool sorting, SLO slider guardrails, and keyboard/a11y. Who can take a look? dan: Skimmed — love the decision tree. Biggest UX question: do we show an explicit "recommended" min/max vs. inline hint? My instinct: show a subtle badge + tooltip rather than forcing a preset. :thinking: elaine: I sketched two treatments — (A) small "recommended" badge next to min/max, tooltip explains basis; (B) inline collapsed suggestion row that you can apply with one click. A is lighter, B is more discoverable. josh: From an implementation POV A is much simpler. For B we need to support transactional apply + undo state in the UI and API change to accept a single apply-recommendation call. Also watch focus management if we insert a new row dynamically. sam: On guardrails: we should prevent min > burst. Also for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity, the guardrail wording must mention SLA impact. Suggest wording: "Guardrail: this setting may increase cost or impact SLAs." mira: Copy options for the burst affordance — current label is just "Burst" which some folks confuse with GPU pool burst. Proposals: "Burst capacity" or "Short-term burst". Thoughts? dan: "Burst capacity" reads clearer to me. Keeps it concise. elaine: Agree on "Burst capacity". Also propose adding microcopy under the control: "Temporarily adds GPUs to meet short spikes (up to X mins)." Keep X dynamic per pool. josh: Accessibility note: ensure burst toggle and the min/max steppers have clear aria-labels. e.g. aria-label="Min vCPUs" is ambiguous — prefer aria-label="Minimum GPUs for this pool" or better: aria-describedby pointing to the help text.
